question.worked_solution:
To find the second derivative of a vector-valued function, we find the second derivatives of the components.

- For $x(t)={t}^{2}+\operatorname{cos}⁡t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =2t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ {x}^{″}(t) & =2-\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

- For $y(t)=t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ {y}^{″}(t) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨{x}^{″}(t),\,{y}^{″}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
